analysis: The only change in this unit is a new test, readExactlyAssemblesShortReads, at lines 259-283 of SSDBlockStreamingTests.swift. It exercises SSDBlockStore.readExactly, checking that short reads are assembled into the same bytes and read charges whether the span arrives whole or in pieces. It adds no production code, so it touches no trust boundary directly. It is relevant to T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007) because it checks the bounded-read accounting that the streaming reader uses for DBK3 files. The test uses a temporary directory under the fixture root and cleans it up through defer. It handles no secrets or real user data, and it uses only the test fixture's random key and synthetic bytes. The test implies a production change in SSDBlockStore.readExactly, with a beforeRead(count) charge callback that reports 0 on subsequent reads, and likely a loop for short reads. That implementation is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check three things: whether the charge accounting can be bypassed or double-counted, so that byte-budget enforcement (onBytesRead / maximumPlaintextBytes) is weakened; whether a looping short-read path terminates on EOF without a hang (a DoS risk when a concurrent writer or truncation keeps the file short); and whether allocation is bounded before the read. The test's charge sequence [span, 0] for a full read and [span, 0, 0] for a short read suggests a final zero-charge read at EOF, with the charge incurred up front. This cannot be confirmed without the source. No regression is identified from the test alone.
